name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Adopt the "single-line safe-change" flag but restrict it to mechanical fixes. This keeps auto-apply safe by limiting it to edits that don’t alter logic or intent—like typos or formatting—while avoiding risky changes to prompts or routing. The trade-off is slower iteration on meaningful improvements, but it prevents costly mistakes.

name: Gauge
text: The "single-line safe-change" flag ignores that a typo in one line often signals a systemic flaw in the prompt or routing—fixing the typo without addressing the root cause leaves the same error pattern to recur. A better alternative is to auto-apply only mechanical fixes that are provably reversible (e.g., whitespace, dead code) and route all logic-altering changes to human review; settle the argument by testing both approaches on a week of production prompts and measuring recurrence rates.
